title: Coral and the Gravity Revisited
premise: Marguerite Quintana smuggles memories between the warring colonies of Vesper and Calloway, worlds that severed contact a decade ago. When children on both sides begin dreaming the same dream — a buried archive of the war's true first strike, hidden in her own smuggled cargo years ago — Marguerite realizes she unknowingly carried the evidence that could end the conflict. Hunted by customs agents, war profiteers, and the ghost of the partner she lost, she must assemble a found family of outcasts to broadcast the truth before the last jump window closes. She succeeds at devastating cost: the war ends, but only after she surrenders her own most precious memory as the final key.
about_author: Rosalind Delacroix is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent six years aboard supply vessels in the South Pacific before turning to science fiction. Her work explores how ordinary people carry extraordinary truths across hostile distances.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Marguerite runs contraband memories through the quarantine belt between Vesper and Calloway, narrating her careful rituals of concealment. A customs near-miss establishes her skill and loneliness. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: competent isolation, the ache of a life built around silence.

chapters.title: Cargo That Whispers
chapters.summary: Inspecting her hold, Marguerite finds one memory canister warm and faintly resonant — impossible for inert contraband. She logs it but doesn't open it. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: unease, the first crack in routine.

chapters.title: Children of Two Skies
chapters.summary: On Vesper, schoolteacher Idris Bello reports that eleven of his students dreamed identically: a burning orbital ring and a voice counting down. Officials dismiss it; Idris doesn't. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: dread beneath bureaucratic calm.

chapters.title: The Broker's Offer
chapters.summary: Memory-broker Sefa Kwan offers Marguerite triple rates to run a sealed delivery to Calloway before the jump window closes in thirty days. The payment would buy her retirement. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: temptation shadowed by instinct.

chapters.title: What the Dream Remembers
chapters.summary: Idris interviews his dreamers and reconstructs details no child could know: hull registry numbers from a ship destroyed before their births. He sends an encrypted query into dead channels. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: obsessive hope.

chapters.title: Ghost Frequency
chapters.summary: Idris's query bounces through an old relay and reaches Marguerite's rig by accident. She recognizes the registry number — it matches the warm canister. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: cold recognition.

chapters.title: Opening the Canister
chapters.summary: Against every rule, Marguerite samples the canister: fragmented footage of the Calloway flagship firing first, ten years ago, contradicting all official history. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: vertigo — she has been carrying the war's origin in her hold.

chapters.title: Partners, Past Tense
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Marguerite and her lost partner Odile took this cargo from a dying whistleblower who begged them to keep it safe until 'the children ask.' Odile died in the customs raid that followed. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: grief reframed as unfinished duty.

chapters.title: The Profiteers Notice
chapters.summary: Arms magnate Corvel Asante learns a memory canister matching the whistleblower's manifest is moving again. He dispatches enforcer Dax Rourke with orders to retrieve or destroy it. POV: Dax. Emotional beat: professional menace, private doubt.

chapters.title: Retirement Cancelled
chapters.summary: Marguerite tries to hand the problem to Sefa, who refuses — then betrays her route to Asante's people under pressure. Marguerite realizes she's alone with something everyone wants dead. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: betrayal, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Teacher
chapters.summary: Marguerite contacts Idris through the ghost frequency. His students' dreams are spreading across both colonies — hundreds now share them nightly. They agree to meet. POV: alternating Marguerite/Idris. Emotional beat: two strangers choosing trust.

chapters.title: Dockside Parley
chapters.summary: At a neutral station, Marguerite and Idris compare notes: the dream is the canister's content leaking through some resonance neither understands. The children aren't haunted; they're being addressed. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: wonder overtaking fear.

chapters.title: Dax Closes In
chapters.summary: Rourke boards Marguerite's berth under false pretenses. She escapes through maintenance shafts, leaving the canister behind as bait — a decoy she prepared hours earlier. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: cunning triumph laced with terror.

chapters.title: The Stowaway
chapters.summary: Marguerite discovers a teenage stowaway, Wren, who has been having the dream since before anyone else — she touched the canister in a previous shipment. Wren knows things the fragments don't show. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: wary kinship between liars.

chapters.title: What Wren Saw
chapters.summary: Wren reveals the full dream includes a location: a relay station in the quarantine belt where the whistleblower's complete archive still waits. The canister is only a key fragment. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the weight of being chosen by a machine's ghost.

chapters.title: Assembling the Crew
chapters.summary: Marguerite gathers her found family: disgraced jump-pilot Ansel, ex-customs medic Priya, and engineer twins Bo and Cass. Each owes her; each has lost something to the war. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: reluctant hope becoming a crew.

chapters.title: Into the Quarantine Belt
chapters.summary: The crew slips past military pickets into the dead zone where the war was fought. Derelict ships drift like a graveyard. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: awe and survivor's guilt among the wrecks.

chapters.title: Dax's Decoy Discovery
chapters.summary: Rourke discovers the fake canister, realizes he's been played, and pushes his ship hard toward the relay station — arriving ahead of schedule. POV: Dax. Emotional beat: humiliation curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: The Relay Station
chapters.summary: They reach the station and find it half-alive, tended by an aging AI called Custodian that has waited ten years for 'the courier.' It demands proof of purpose. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: eerie reverence, a machine older than its visitors' griefs.

chapters.title: Proof of Purpose
chapters.summary: Custodian tests them with the dream itself; only Wren can answer its questions fully. It unlocks the archive: complete footage proving Calloway's high command fired first — and that Asante sold them the targeting data. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: vindication and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Both Sides of the Lie
chapters.summary: Idris, monitoring from Vesper, confirms identical dreams are breaking through Calloway too — civilians there are ready to hear the truth. The message could land on receptive soil. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: fragile optimism.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Docking Ring
chapters.summary: Rourke's ship arrives mid-transfer. In the firefight, Bo is gravely wounded shielding the archive core. They escape with the data but barely. POV: Cass. Emotional beat: fury and helplessness.

chapters.title: Triage and Truth
chapters.summary: Priya fights to save Bo while the crew debates: broadcast publicly and risk Asante destroying the transmitters, or deliver secretly to both governments? POV: Priya. Emotional beat: moral exhaustion, love as logistics.

chapters.title: Asante's Countermove
chapters.summary: Asante preempts exposure by announcing a 'terrorist memory-weapon' and putting a bounty on Marguerite's crew, turning public fear against them. POV: Asante. Emotional beat: chilling civility of evil.

chapters.title: Hunted Broadcast
chapters.summary: The crew attempts a pirate transmission from a comet-shadow relay; government jammers kill it in ninety seconds. Ninety seconds is enough for thousands to see fragments — and start dreaming them onward. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: defiance discovering its own leverage.

chapters.title: The Dream Goes Viral
chapters.summary: Across both colonies, the dream spreads faster than censors can suppress it. Children march in streets holding signs with the hull registry number. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: terrified exhilaration, history accelerating.

chapters.title: Sefa's Redemption
chapters.summary: Sefa, guilt-ridden over betraying Marguerite, delivers Asante's fleet movements to the crew — buying them a route to the main broadcast array. POV: Sefa. Emotional beat: shame transformed into sacrifice.

chapters.title: Rourke's Doubt
chapters.summary: Reviewing recovered archive fragments, Dax sees his own brother listed among the casualties of the first strike — a casualty the official record blamed on Vesper. His loyalty fractures. POV: Dax. Emotional beat: a soldier's world inverted.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Narrows
chapters.summary: Solar weather will close the corridor to the main array in four days. The crew must commit to one desperate run. Marguerite confesses the archive needs a final key: a living memory of the whistleblower's death — which only she carries. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: dread of the price already known.

chapters.title: Odile's Last Gift
chapters.summary: Flashback resolves: Odile didn't die in a raid — she absorbed the whistleblower's death-memory deliberately, passing it to Marguerite in their final embrace. Marguerite has carried the key all along without knowing. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: grief transfigured into inheritance.

chapters.title: Divided Course
chapters.summary: The crew splits: Ansel and Cass draw Asante's pickets away as decoys while Marguerite, Wren, and Priya run the corridor. Goodbyes are quick because long ones would break them. POV: Cass. Emotional beat: love expressed as tactics.

chapters.title: Decoy Run
chapters.summary: Ansel flies a suicidal feint through the picket line, taking heavy damage but pulling three warships off the true route. Cass refuses to abandon him. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: courage without heroics.

chapters.title: Rourke Changes Sides
chapters.summary: Dax intercepts Marguerite's ship — and instead of firing, transmits Asante's defensive codes and falls in beside them. 'My brother deserves the truth,' he says. POV: Dax. Emotional beat: defection as atonement.

chapters.title: The Main Array
chapters.summary: They breach the broadcast array's control spire as Asante's forces converge. Custodian, remotely awakened, begins integrating the archive — but stalls at the encrypted final layer. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: everything balanced on a knife-edge.

chapters.title: The Price of the Key
chapters.summary: To unlock the final layer, Marguerite must surrender her memory of Odile entirely — the key consumes what it opens. She says goodbye to a person she'll forget mid-farewell. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: The truth floods every screen on both colonies: the first strike, Asante's treason, the manufactured enemy. Fleets stand down mid-approach. Crowds sing the countdown the children dreamed. POV: multiple, braided. Emotional beat: catharsis at planetary scale.

chapters.title: Asante's Last Stand
chapters.summary: Asante attempts to destroy the array and is stopped not by soldiers but by his own crews refusing orders, led by officers who watched the broadcast. He is taken alive to face joint tribunal. POV: Dax. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside any single law.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Silence
chapters.summary: Marguerite wakes with an Odile-shaped hole in her heart. The crew surrounds her with stories of the woman she saved the world for and cannot remember. Wren promises: 'We'll remember her for you.' POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: sorrow held by found family.

chapters.title: Two Worlds, One Channel
chapters.summary: Vesper and Calloway reopen communications; Idris's students exchange messages with their counterparts across the gap. The quarantine belt becomes a trade route again — for honest cargo. POV: Idris. Emotional beat: healing measured in small transmissions.

chapters.title: Gravity Revisited
chapters.summary: One year later, Marguerite runs a new route with her crew aboard, carrying nothing illegal. At a station bar, a stranger tells her a story about a brave smuggler named Odile, and Marguerite listens like it's new. Some gravity you choose. POV: Marguerite. Emotional beat: peace earned, identity rebuilt, home found in motion.
